I'm ok with this, but these naming schemes are Meta specified but the components are off-the-shelf devices.  We might not be able to change the sensor names like this.

Alexander was potentially working on a method to overwrite common-device configs on a per-machine basis, which could be leveraged in the future.  Until that is in, unless this naming change is acceptable upstream, we might need to keep these as a patch downstream.

CompatibleHardware + config record includes could be abused to make this possible.

https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/entity-manager/+/79657
https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/entity-manager/+/77496

But it's not really the best use for it since an EM config still describes a piece of hardware. Config record includes were meant to cover the use-case for board variants, but renaming a sensor is not a hardware variant. It would be possible but there might be pushback.

Alternatively, Meta could propose a naming scheme for sensor names and document it in EM repo?

@ed@tanous.net @spinler@us.ibm.com Do you have any input on the sensor names?

https://www.dmtf.org/sites/default/files/standards/documents/DSP2049_0.2.2b.pdf

could be used as the starting point since it already defines some sensor names from the redfish side.
Yes, the config record includes is what I was thinking of.  I don't think Meta should be dictating a "consistent" sensor naming schema.

> I don't think Meta should be dictating a "consistent" sensor naming schema.

Not dictating, more like

"if you want a guideline on how to name this sensor, here is a sane solution"

A document like that could provide guidance in case people want to modify common configs.

And provide some guarantees for people that if they edit common configs, it is acceptable to adjust the names to match the conventional style.

Otherwise tomorrow HPE (or someone else) comes along to edit ```cx7_ocp.json``` to fit their naming preference and then your downstream patch breaks 😄

> Do you have any input on the sensor names?

Original intent of EM was that it follow the naming convention put in this patch.

"NIC 1 Temperature" which is what humans read.  Since then lots of companies have used EM files as their canvas for applying naming conventions, in some extremes even modifying the EM code (downstream) to allow applying naming conventions that weren't even supported and would cause backward compatibility issues.
 
I'm not in love with trying to prescribe any one companies naming convention in these files, but unfortunately they do define the external (redfish/IPMI) API names currently.  I'd much prefer that we have one consistent human facing way of representing the files, and intelligent conversion functions if we need to apply "Meta naming" or "Nvidia naming" conventions to things that differs.

But how much that matters?  I'm not willing to spend effort on it, so I'll accept whatever naming everyone can agree on.  I will say I'm not a fan of the "whomever checked it in first wins" approach and would like to see some consistency here, but consistency is hard.

> "NIC 1 Temperature" which is what humans read. 

We (Meta) don't have humans.  😊

Everything goes through automation and unfortunately our internal team has a "sensor schema we want to see".  This is easy for content under `configurations/meta` but is obviously less easy for stuff outside there.

> I will say I'm not a fan of the "whomever checked it in first wins" approach and would like to see some consistency here, but consistency is hard.

I agree with the sentiment and would like to see consistency.  I think there is some value in "first mover gets preference" though when we're the ones putting in the effort to do everything upstream.  We've even contributed most of the configs for Nvidia hardware.

I brought up @alexander.hansen@9elements.com 's work because Meta has been contracting with 9E to improve the situation here with this exact problem in mind.  There has been work in this direction but I don't think the [upstream] reception has been great.

I'm fine with holding downstream patches for stuff that is in common use (like Nvidia parts) but I don't think we should need to hold downstream patches when we seem to be the only one using the config (as is the case of the Broadcomm ones) and we're the ones expending the effort on both ends of this problem: contributing the hardware configs and trying to enhance EM to have vendor/platform-specific tweaks.

As soon as Alexander's work is in an acceptable state, I'm good with us refactoring every sensor to be a "human-oriented name" if that's what you want and then the Meta-schema can be handled with his work.
Names shouldn't include underscores.
We've named all of our sensors this way.

Why the `_C` ?

Why are we making the sensor unit part of the sensor name?

The sensor value interface already provides the unit.

That's just how our internal teams at Meta have previously specified the schema for sensors.  All the sensors for all the servers end up in a big database that people can run queries against and there is a common schema for those names to make it easier to run similar queries against different platforms.

Changing the name will break anyone who had this exact use-case (storing the values in a database) since their sensor name will change.

Also it will break folks who are testing their redfish response to contain exactly this sensor name which they expect to be present.

And likely a different user of this config will have a different naming scheme.

Some may like to name the sensor the same as in the schematics.

Nothing is stable in this complete mess 😄


That being said, my question is answered (thanks!), i do not have anything for or against this change, but a documented naming convention would be nice.

This could even be in ```configurations/meta/SENSOR_NAMES.md```, just to point people towards 'something'.

If upstream does not come up with some alternative, at least there is some reference in the repo with a rationale for how meta go to the point of suffixing units onto sensor names 😄, and why that's part of some common configs.
